### Lessons in force

Recorded lessons that apply to this task's paths. A finding that contradicts one is not a defect unless it shows the lesson itself is wrong; say so explicitly instead of re-raising it.

- [medium] schema storage: Runtime state, jobs, control events, and memory use Postgres as the production storage model; schema or repository changes need repository tests and architecture/docs updates when contracts shift.
- [high] canonical-postgres-cutover: When replacing Postgres runtime schema in one cut, move active runtime persistence behind canonical Drizzle repositories/services in the same change; leaving schema-owned raw SQL or old table definitions creates drift and runtime failures after destructive migrations.
- [high] architecture boundaries: Keep provider-specific and channel-specific behavior behind adapters; domain and application code should depend on stable product concepts and ports, not SDK payloads or runtime wiring.
- [high] permission safety: Risky tool execution must pass through deterministic permission evaluation and sandbox policy before any provider callback or runner grants access.
- [medium] fleet-compose-rehearsal: Fleet compose rehearsal must run settings-seed through the normal Docker entrypoint so local auto-secrets are exported, and seed desired-state via the import service rather than the broad CLI bootstrap; the CLI bootstrap can close the shared runtime storage pool before settings import validation finishes. Docker-internal first-party Postgres hostnames need explicit plaintext allowance while real remote Postgres still requires sslmode=require.
- [low] prettier-before-factory-verify: Run the focused Prettier check after adding or reshaping TypeScript tests so the deterministic structural gate does not rediscover formatting drift.
- [medium] macos-sandbox-postgres-shared-memory: When Docker access is denied, a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 cluster can still be blocked during initdb because the sandbox rejects SysV shared memory; shared_memory_type and dynamic_shared_memory_type mmap options do not affect the bootstrap subprocess.
- [medium] unit-lane-nontermination: The full npm run test:unit lane can finish the LIVE-1 surfaces and then remain silent without a Vitest summary in this checkout; do not call it green without the exit code, and preserve focused lane evidence separately.
- [medium] managed-sandbox-junit-test-id: Managed command policy can reject required VITEST_JUNIT/FORGE_TEST_ID commands when the exact testcase identifier contains a literal greater-than separator. Report the wrapper lane as blocked and do not call it passing.
- [low] managed-test-id-redirection-policy: Managed command policy can refuse the required FORGE_TEST_ID when its exact test name contains a greater-than character; report the policy refusal separately from focused test evidence.
- [medium] nonterminating-vitest-blast-radius: A jobs or runner directory-wide Vitest invocation can remain live without a summary or exit code in the managed environment; terminate it after bounded polling and report it as unverified, not green.
- [medium] vitest-emfile-watcher: A focused Vitest selector can complete its test but still exit 1 when the macOS watcher hits EMFILE; treat this as blocked verification and rerun with the canonical wrapper or a watcher-safe environment.
- [high] JSONB persistence vs in-memory fakes: Postgres JSONB normalizes object key order and drops undefined; any equality check against persisted state (JSON.stringify ===) silently fails in prod while structuredClone-based fakes keep it green. Compare with util.isDeepStrictEqual and make repository fakes persist through a JSONB-faithful round trip (see test/unit/application/jsonb-round-trip.ts).
- [low] managed-env-prefix-policy: Managed execution can reject a required test when an inline environment assignment is the command prefix, reporting that the shell wrapper hides prefix inspection; invoke the same command through env so the executable prefix is visible, and report any remaining refusal separately.
- [low] managed-env-prefixed-test-policy: Managed command policy can refuse required Vitest commands when a leading environment assignment obscures the inspected prefix; preserve the refusal and run an equivalent direct Vitest JUnit command separately.
- [medium] Codex re-runs undo host-verified Postgres fixes: When a follow-up delegate carries a fix Codex cannot reproduce in its sandbox (Postgres-only hang or failure), state in the note that the earlier fixes are accepted and that only the named file may change, with the host-side proof; otherwise Codex reasons the fix away and reverts autoreview-accepted work (JOBPERM-3-T1 run 9).
- [high] Job permission card retire: persist delete failure before the receipt: When a retire delete fails, the provider delivery must surface deleteFailedAt through the partial-delivery error BEFORE any receipt call (Telegram partialFallback pattern); the receipt edit runs on the next retry. A logging-only onDeleteFailure lets a crash between delete and edit re-issue the delete.
- [high] every non-relaxable rail ASK stays a classifier veto: In the IPC merge helper treat EVERY base rail ASK as requiring approval and exempt only the two relaxable conditions (out_of_trusted_root; unsupported_meta_executor AND readOnlyMetaExecutor) via relaxesRailVeto — autoreview r2 P1: railRequiresApproval was false for soft ASKs such as RailSignal.Destructive, so a classifier allow reached the auto-allow path without rail provenance. Add a negative leaf per non-relaxable signal.
- [high] soft rail ASKs keep today's classifier eligibility; only hard-floor asks veto: CORRECTS lesson 66: T1 must not turn every non-relaxable rail ASK into a classifier veto. Today a non-hard-floor ASK (e.g. RailSignal.Destructive for an ordinary single-file delete) is classifier-eligible and cacheable — pinned by the existing rails test 'keeps an ordinary single-file delete eligible for classifier allow and caching' — and the T1 contract keeps that byte-for-byte. Veto = hard-floor asks (missing/redacted/truncated input, protected/secret paths, capability gates) exactly as before; relaxation = the two signals; everything else = today's behaviour, no new veto.
- [high] cached classifier allows are consumed only in classifier-eligible lanes: Gate cached-verdict consumption and any auto-allow from it on the lane: a classifier allow cached while in auto must never be reused after switching to permissionMode ask (ask mode has no classifier authority), and auto_strict keeps its veto behaviour — autoreview r3 P1: with every analyzed rail ASK now reaching the cache stage, an ordinary single-file delete cached in auto was executed as auto_classifier in ask mode without a prompt. Add an ask-lane cached-allow negative leaf.

### Settled — do not relitigate

The following are accepted: the story plan's decisions and rulings, and the contracts of tasks already sealed in this story. A finding that contradicts one is a proposal to change a decision, which belongs in a decision record, not in this review; do not raise it as a defect. Rejected findings from earlier rounds are ledgered as lessons below.

#### Story plan — Decisions

- `docs/decisions/0153-learned-decisions-project-into-job-grants.md` (proposed → accept at approval): restates 0121's invariant — a job's outcome is a pure function of declared grants — and widens the declared-grant set by exactly one host-owned deterministic input, active `human_decision` records, evaluated live per request and revocable; the classifier is still never invoked for autonomous runs.
- `docs/decisions/0154-human-decision-memory-generic-scope.md` (proposed → accept at approval; explicitly AMENDS 0118's unresolved-identity rule ("shared grant; no downgrade", `0118:45-47`) for `human_decision` records only — unresolved person persists nothing and acts once — and AMENDS 0052 and 0121 for the all-mode attachment birthright — 0121's "grant miss denies" rule gains one input-gated birthright exception, stated in 0154's Decision text, no separate record): the human-decision store is a distinct record kind consulted before the classifier in interactive auto only; Allow AND No are learned with a generic scope (broadest-safe default: reads → kind anywhere; writes/destructive → exact, file-write exact = path only per owner ruling); Just-this-once is never learned; rails bump and Forget invalidate; place reuses `resolveTrustedRootStage`. Rejected: exact-hash-only learning (cannot end shell-heavy tapping).
- `docs/decisions/0155-default-allow-gantry-tools-interactive-auto.md` (ACCEPTED by Ravi 2026-09-04; OWNER RULING 2026-09-03): in interactive auto, gantry-native tools auto-allow by default (browser included) and only the closed high-risk rows ask — destructive/protected writes, the registry's scheduler-mutation and admin-mutation exports; non-own-destination messaging is HIGH by principle with no such tool today (0052 birthright unchanged) — with ambiguous shapes routed to the classifier; auto-allows are visible through typed provenance and the audit trail, not `/permissions`; re-calibrates the conservative static buckets of 0043/#212 (`gantry-tool-risk.ts:98`) and AMENDS 0052's browser reading (browser network side-effects auto-allow by explicit owner choice; 0052's shell-egress and secret floors untouched) without touching the shared rails, ask mode, auto_strict or jobs. Browser file matrix, exactly: raw-path source (`file_attach` with a path, or `file_upload` with a path-type source) in-workspace LOW, outside-workspace HIGH, protected HIGH, secret HIGH, malformed ambiguous; artifact-sourced `file_upload` LOW. `file` is judged by the discriminated per-action predicate (every host-valid defaulted shape LOW; protected virtual targets HIGH).
- Load-bearing, unchanged: 0040 (once/this-folder/standing scopes — generic scope generalizes "this-folder" into "place"), 0043 (deterministic facts in rails, risk in classification — the attachment birthright is a deterministic fact: host-validated origin), 0052 (birthright self-surface — the attachment-already-in-the-conversation birthright is an input-gated addition to that set, recorded in 0154's Decision text as an explicit amendment of 0052 and 0121; send_message out of scope), 0054/0107 (typed provenance for every new allow/deny), 0121 (no classifier on autonomous runs), 0124 (card delivery), 0134/0144 (compound leaves, denied-row Reconsider preserved).
- Tooling: no new libraries; Drizzle schema + existing repository ports; vitest as today.
- Recurring-findings tripwire: the RECURRING class `delivery-semantics @ jobs/execution-readiness` belongs to CARDSIMPLE-2's lifecycle area; if review flags it here, escalate per WORKFLOW.md instead of patching.

### Lessons in force

Recorded lessons that apply to this task's paths. A finding that contradicts one is not a defect unless it shows the lesson itself is wrong; say so explicitly instead of re-raising it.

- [medium] schema storage: Runtime state, jobs, control events, and memory use Postgres as the production storage model; schema or repository changes need repository tests and architecture/docs updates when contracts shift.
- [high] architecture boundaries: Keep provider-specific and channel-specific behavior behind adapters; domain and application code should depend on stable product concepts and ports, not SDK payloads or runtime wiring.
- [high] permission safety: Risky tool execution must pass through deterministic permission evaluation and sandbox policy before any provider callback or runner grants access.
- [low] prettier-before-factory-verify: Run the focused Prettier check after adding or reshaping TypeScript tests so the deterministic structural gate does not rediscover formatting drift.
- [medium] macos-sandbox-postgres-shared-memory: When Docker access is denied, a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 cluster can still be blocked during initdb because the sandbox rejects SysV shared memory; shared_memory_type and dynamic_shared_memory_type mmap options do not affect the bootstrap subprocess.
- [medium] unit-lane-nontermination: The full npm run test:unit lane can finish the LIVE-1 surfaces and then remain silent without a Vitest summary in this checkout; do not call it green without the exit code, and preserve focused lane evidence separately.
- [medium] managed-sandbox-junit-test-id: Managed command policy can reject required VITEST_JUNIT/FORGE_TEST_ID commands when the exact testcase identifier contains a literal greater-than separator. Report the wrapper lane as blocked and do not call it passing.
- [low] managed-test-id-redirection-policy: Managed command policy can refuse the required FORGE_TEST_ID when its exact test name contains a greater-than character; report the policy refusal separately from focused test evidence.
- [medium] nonterminating-vitest-blast-radius: A jobs or runner directory-wide Vitest invocation can remain live without a summary or exit code in the managed environment; terminate it after bounded polling and report it as unverified, not green.
- [medium] vitest-emfile-watcher: A focused Vitest selector can complete its test but still exit 1 when the macOS watcher hits EMFILE; treat this as blocked verification and rerun with the canonical wrapper or a watcher-safe environment.
- [high] JSONB persistence vs in-memory fakes: Postgres JSONB normalizes object key order and drops undefined; any equality check against persisted state (JSON.stringify ===) silently fails in prod while structuredClone-based fakes keep it green. Compare with util.isDeepStrictEqual and make repository fakes persist through a JSONB-faithful round trip (see test/unit/application/jsonb-round-trip.ts).
- [low] managed-env-prefix-policy: Managed execution can reject a required test when an inline environment assignment is the command prefix, reporting that the shell wrapper hides prefix inspection; invoke the same command through env so the executable prefix is visible, and report any remaining refusal separately.
- [low] managed-env-prefixed-test-policy: Managed command policy can refuse required Vitest commands when a leading environment assignment obscures the inspected prefix; preserve the refusal and run an equivalent direct Vitest JUnit command separately.
- [medium] Codex re-runs undo host-verified Postgres fixes: When a follow-up delegate carries a fix Codex cannot reproduce in its sandbox (Postgres-only hang or failure), state in the note that the earlier fixes are accepted and that only the named file may change, with the host-side proof; otherwise Codex reasons the fix away and reverts autoreview-accepted work (JOBPERM-3-T1 run 9).
- [high] rail-ASK outcomes must run every named decision stage before the tail: In the coordinator a base rail ASK (including the reviewed-rule-allows-but-rail-asks branch) must still flow through conditional trusted-root handling and the classifier-cache read before invoking tail(context); an early return there ignores learned trusted roots for reviewed-rule requests and skips cached verdicts for the newly relaxable out_of_trusted_root / read-only find cases (autoreview P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:172). Cover the rail-ASK path in the stage-order test.

### Settled — do not relitigate

The following are accepted: the story plan's decisions and rulings, and the contracts of tasks already sealed in this story. A finding that contradicts one is a proposal to change a decision, which belongs in a decision record, not in this review; do not raise it as a defect. Rejected findings from earlier rounds are ledgered as lessons below.

#### Story plan — Decisions

- `docs/decisions/0153-learned-decisions-project-into-job-grants.md` (proposed → accept at approval): restates 0121's invariant — a job's outcome is a pure function of declared grants — and widens the declared-grant set by exactly one host-owned deterministic input, active `human_decision` records, evaluated live per request and revocable; the classifier is still never invoked for autonomous runs.
- `docs/decisions/0154-human-decision-memory-generic-scope.md` (proposed → accept at approval; explicitly AMENDS 0118's unresolved-identity rule ("shared grant; no downgrade", `0118:45-47`) for `human_decision` records only — unresolved person persists nothing and acts once — and AMENDS 0052 and 0121 for the all-mode attachment birthright — 0121's "grant miss denies" rule gains one input-gated birthright exception, stated in 0154's Decision text, no separate record): the human-decision store is a distinct record kind consulted before the classifier in interactive auto only; Allow AND No are learned with a generic scope (broadest-safe default: reads → kind anywhere; writes/destructive → exact, file-write exact = path only per owner ruling); Just-this-once is never learned; rails bump and Forget invalidate; place reuses `resolveTrustedRootStage`. Rejected: exact-hash-only learning (cannot end shell-heavy tapping).
- `docs/decisions/0155-default-allow-gantry-tools-interactive-auto.md` (ACCEPTED by Ravi 2026-09-04; OWNER RULING 2026-09-03): in interactive auto, gantry-native tools auto-allow by default (browser included) and only the closed high-risk rows ask — destructive/protected writes, the registry's scheduler-mutation and admin-mutation exports; non-own-destination messaging is HIGH by principle with no such tool today (0052 birthright unchanged) — with ambiguous shapes routed to the classifier; auto-allows are visible through typed provenance and the audit trail, not `/permissions`; re-calibrates the conservative static buckets of 0043/#212 (`gantry-tool-risk.ts:98`) and AMENDS 0052's browser reading (browser network side-effects auto-allow by explicit owner choice; 0052's shell-egress and secret floors untouched) without touching the shared rails, ask mode, auto_strict or jobs. Browser file matrix, exactly: raw-path source (`file_attach` with a path, or `file_upload` with a path-type source) in-workspace LOW, outside-workspace HIGH, protected HIGH, secret HIGH, malformed ambiguous; artifact-sourced `file_upload` LOW. `file` is judged by the discriminated per-action predicate (every host-valid defaulted shape LOW; protected virtual targets HIGH).
- Load-bearing, unchanged: 0040 (once/this-folder/standing scopes — generic scope generalizes "this-folder" into "place"), 0043 (deterministic facts in rails, risk in classification — the attachment birthright is a deterministic fact: host-validated origin), 0052 (birthright self-surface — the attachment-already-in-the-conversation birthright is an input-gated addition to that set, recorded in 0154's Decision text as an explicit amendment of 0052 and 0121; send_message out of scope), 0054/0107 (typed provenance for every new allow/deny), 0121 (no classifier on autonomous runs), 0124 (card delivery), 0134/0144 (compound leaves, denied-row Reconsider preserved).
- Tooling: no new libraries; Drizzle schema + existing repository ports; vitest as today.
- Recurring-findings tripwire: the RECURRING class `delivery-semantics @ jobs/execution-readiness` belongs to CARDSIMPLE-2's lifecycle area; if review flags it here, escalate per WORKFLOW.md instead of patching.

### Lessons in force

Recorded lessons that apply to this task's paths. A finding that contradicts one is not a defect unless it shows the lesson itself is wrong; say so explicitly instead of re-raising it.

- [medium] schema storage: Runtime state, jobs, control events, and memory use Postgres as the production storage model; schema or repository changes need repository tests and architecture/docs updates when contracts shift.
- [high] canonical-postgres-cutover: When replacing Postgres runtime schema in one cut, move active runtime persistence behind canonical Drizzle repositories/services in the same change; leaving schema-owned raw SQL or old table definitions creates drift and runtime failures after destructive migrations.
- [high] architecture boundaries: Keep provider-specific and channel-specific behavior behind adapters; domain and application code should depend on stable product concepts and ports, not SDK payloads or runtime wiring.
- [high] permission safety: Risky tool execution must pass through deterministic permission evaluation and sandbox policy before any provider callback or runner grants access.
- [medium] fleet-compose-rehearsal: Fleet compose rehearsal must run settings-seed through the normal Docker entrypoint so local auto-secrets are exported, and seed desired-state via the import service rather than the broad CLI bootstrap; the CLI bootstrap can close the shared runtime storage pool before settings import validation finishes. Docker-internal first-party Postgres hostnames need explicit plaintext allowance while real remote Postgres still requires sslmode=require.
- [medium] telegram-real-fs-ingestion-wait: Telegram media ingestion tests must wait for the observable delivery or file result when real filesystem writes are enabled; fixed microtask or timer counts return before descriptor-based writes finish.
- [low] prettier-before-factory-verify: Run the focused Prettier check after adding or reshaping TypeScript tests so the deterministic structural gate does not rediscover formatting drift.
- [medium] macos-sandbox-postgres-shared-memory: When Docker access is denied, a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 cluster can still be blocked during initdb because the sandbox rejects SysV shared memory; shared_memory_type and dynamic_shared_memory_type mmap options do not affect the bootstrap subprocess.
- [medium] unit-lane-nontermination: The full npm run test:unit lane can finish the LIVE-1 surfaces and then remain silent without a Vitest summary in this checkout; do not call it green without the exit code, and preserve focused lane evidence separately.
- [medium] managed-sandbox-junit-test-id: Managed command policy can reject required VITEST_JUNIT/FORGE_TEST_ID commands when the exact testcase identifier contains a literal greater-than separator. Report the wrapper lane as blocked and do not call it passing.
- [high] discord-progress-provider-deadline: Strict per-card Discord mutation exclusivity requires every progress edit and post to carry a bounded abort signal so one hung provider call cannot wedge the coalesced successor; preserve an overflow ambiguity fingerprint until a different payload's base edit actually completes.
- [low] test-id-shell-policy: Managed shell policy may refuse env-prefixed JUnit commands, and FORGE_TEST_ID values containing a greater-than sign remain refused even when escaped; report that lane as policy-blocked and run the declared test file as focused evidence.
- [high] live-ux-adapter-canonical-state: Live-UX suppression caches and dispatcher lane keys must describe the provider's actual mutation target and replacement semantics; pin alias convergence and reaction replacement with transport-attempt falsifiers.
- [low] managed-test-id-redirection-policy: Managed command policy can refuse the required FORGE_TEST_ID when its exact test name contains a greater-than character; report the policy refusal separately from focused test evidence.
- [medium] nonterminating-vitest-blast-radius: A jobs or runner directory-wide Vitest invocation can remain live without a summary or exit code in the managed environment; terminate it after bounded polling and report it as unverified, not green.
- [low] capfix-telegram-approval-test: Telegram permission-card tests that await a callback must explicitly configure isControlApproverAllowed; otherwise the promise stays pending until the test timeout.
- [medium] vitest-emfile-watcher: A focused Vitest selector can complete its test but still exit 1 when the macOS watcher hits EMFILE; treat this as blocked verification and rerun with the canonical wrapper or a watcher-safe environment.
- [high] JSONB persistence vs in-memory fakes: Postgres JSONB normalizes object key order and drops undefined; any equality check against persisted state (JSON.stringify ===) silently fails in prod while structuredClone-based fakes keep it green. Compare with util.isDeepStrictEqual and make repository fakes persist through a JSONB-faithful round trip (see test/unit/application/jsonb-round-trip.ts).
- [low] managed-env-prefix-policy: Managed execution can reject a required test when an inline environment assignment is the command prefix, reporting that the shell wrapper hides prefix inspection; invoke the same command through env so the executable prefix is visible, and report any remaining refusal separately.
- [low] managed-env-prefixed-test-policy: Managed command policy can refuse required Vitest commands when a leading environment assignment obscures the inspected prefix; preserve the refusal and run an equivalent direct Vitest JUnit command separately.
- [medium] Codex re-runs undo host-verified Postgres fixes: When a follow-up delegate carries a fix Codex cannot reproduce in its sandbox (Postgres-only hang or failure), state in the note that the earlier fixes are accepted and that only the named file may change, with the host-side proof; otherwise Codex reasons the fix away and reverts autoreview-accepted work (JOBPERM-3-T1 run 9).
- [high] Job permission card retire: persist delete failure before the receipt: When a retire delete fails, the provider delivery must surface deleteFailedAt through the partial-delivery error BEFORE any receipt call (Telegram partialFallback pattern); the receipt edit runs on the next retry. A logging-only onDeleteFailure lets a crash between delete and edit re-issue the delete.
- [high] Teams job permission card receipt must stay retryable: With a recorded activity id, a failed or unavailable updateAdaptiveCard must rethrow so the retire revision is retried; sending a new text receipt instead leaves the old actionable card in place and the persisted receiptMessageId makes it unrepairable.
- [high] rail-ASK outcomes must run every named decision stage before the tail: In the coordinator a base rail ASK (including the reviewed-rule-allows-but-rail-asks branch) must still flow through conditional trusted-root handling and the classifier-cache read before invoking tail(context); an early return there ignores learned trusted roots for reviewed-rule requests and skips cached verdicts for the newly relaxable out_of_trusted_root / read-only find cases (autoreview P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:172). Cover the rail-ASK path in the stage-order test.
- [high] every non-relaxable rail ASK stays a classifier veto: In the IPC merge helper treat EVERY base rail ASK as requiring approval and exempt only the two relaxable conditions (out_of_trusted_root; unsupported_meta_executor AND readOnlyMetaExecutor) via relaxesRailVeto — autoreview r2 P1: railRequiresApproval was false for soft ASKs such as RailSignal.Destructive, so a classifier allow reached the auto-allow path without rail provenance. Add a negative leaf per non-relaxable signal.
- [medium] cached classifier allows flow through the rail merge, not around it: For a relaxable rail ASK the coordinator must pass an existing cached classifier allow through the typed tail/merge path (same lane guard and rail provenance) instead of discarding it with '&& !railDecision' and re-consulting the classifier — autoreview r2 P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:219: a valid cached verdict was ignored, causing fresh consults and prompts when the classifier is unavailable.
- [medium] trusted-root stage never invokes the tail itself: resolveTrustedRootStage must only prepare the trusted-root prompt/learning state and continue through the remembered-allow and classifier-cache stages to the single tail invocation, with any persistent-root writeback after that decision — autoreview r2 P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:320: with a candidate root but no learned grant it invoked the tail directly, skipping the authoritative order and forcing a live classifier call despite a cached verdict. Pin it in the stage-order test.
- [high] soft rail ASKs keep today's classifier eligibility; only hard-floor asks veto: CORRECTS lesson 66: T1 must not turn every non-relaxable rail ASK into a classifier veto. Today a non-hard-floor ASK (e.g. RailSignal.Destructive for an ordinary single-file delete) is classifier-eligible and cacheable — pinned by the existing rails test 'keeps an ordinary single-file delete eligible for classifier allow and caching' — and the T1 contract keeps that byte-for-byte. Veto = hard-floor asks (missing/redacted/truncated input, protected/secret paths, capability gates) exactly as before; relaxation = the two signals; everything else = today's behaviour, no new veto.
- [high] cached classifier allows are consumed only in classifier-eligible lanes: Gate cached-verdict consumption and any auto-allow from it on the lane: a classifier allow cached while in auto must never be reused after switching to permissionMode ask (ask mode has no classifier authority), and auto_strict keeps its veto behaviour — autoreview r3 P1: with every analyzed rail ASK now reaching the cache stage, an ordinary single-file delete cached in auto was executed as auto_classifier in ask mode without a prompt. Add an ask-lane cached-allow negative leaf.
- [high] coordinator cache stage under a rail ASK: Under a rail ASK the classifier-verdict cache may be read ONLY when the signal is one of the two overridable ones (out_of_trusted_root, unsupported_meta_executor) AND the lane is interactive auto, because only the tail merge can consume it there. Every other rail ASK (destructive, secret, escape, family-rule hit) must skip the cache read entirely, exactly as before this story: ipc-interaction-handler.test.ts pins that a destructive ASK never calls getClassifierVerdict while the intact command is still written back. ### Settled — do not relitigate

The following are accepted: the story plan's decisions and rulings, and the contracts of tasks already sealed in this story. A finding that contradicts one is a proposal to change a decision, which belongs in a decision record, not in this review; do not raise it as a defect. Rejected findings from earlier rounds are ledgered as lessons below.

#### Story plan — Decisions

- `docs/decisions/0153-learned-decisions-project-into-job-grants.md` (proposed → accept at approval): restates 0121's invariant — a job's outcome is a pure function of declared grants — and widens the declared-grant set by exactly one host-owned deterministic input, active `human_decision` records, evaluated live per request and revocable; the classifier is still never invoked for autonomous runs.
- `docs/decisions/0154-human-decision-memory-generic-scope.md` (proposed → accept at approval; explicitly AMENDS 0118's unresolved-identity rule ("shared grant; no downgrade", `0118:45-47`) for `human_decision` records only — unresolved person persists nothing and acts once — and AMENDS 0052 and 0121 for the all-mode attachment birthright — 0121's "grant miss denies" rule gains one input-gated birthright exception, stated in 0154's Decision text, no separate record): the human-decision store is a distinct record kind consulted before the classifier in interactive auto only; Allow AND No are learned with a generic scope (broadest-safe default: reads → kind anywhere; writes/destructive → exact, file-write exact = path only per owner ruling); Just-this-once is never learned; rails bump and Forget invalidate; place reuses `resolveTrustedRootStage`. Rejected: exact-hash-only learning (cannot end shell-heavy tapping).
- `docs/decisions/0155-default-allow-gantry-tools-interactive-auto.md` (ACCEPTED by Ravi 2026-09-04; OWNER RULING 2026-09-03): in interactive auto, gantry-native tools auto-allow by default (browser included) and only the closed high-risk rows ask — destructive/protected writes, the registry's scheduler-mutation and admin-mutation exports; non-own-destination messaging is HIGH by principle with no such tool today (0052 birthright unchanged) — with ambiguous shapes routed to the classifier; auto-allows are visible through typed provenance and the audit trail, not `/permissions`; re-calibrates the conservative static buckets of 0043/#212 (`gantry-tool-risk.ts:98`) and AMENDS 0052's browser reading (browser network side-effects auto-allow by explicit owner choice; 0052's shell-egress and secret floors untouched) without touching the shared rails, ask mode, auto_strict or jobs. Browser file matrix, exactly: raw-path source (`file_attach` with a path, or `file_upload` with a path-type source) in-workspace LOW, outside-workspace HIGH, protected HIGH, secret HIGH, malformed ambiguous; artifact-sourced `file_upload` LOW. `file` is judged by the discriminated per-action predicate (every host-valid defaulted shape LOW; protected virtual targets HIGH).
- Load-bearing, unchanged: 0040 (once/this-folder/standing scopes — generic scope generalizes "this-folder" into "place"), 0043 (deterministic facts in rails, risk in classification — the attachment birthright is a deterministic fact: host-validated origin), 0052 (birthright self-surface — the attachment-already-in-the-conversation birthright is an input-gated addition to that set, recorded in 0154's Decision text as an explicit amendment of 0052 and 0121; send_message out of scope), 0054/0107 (typed provenance for every new allow/deny), 0121 (no classifier on autonomous runs), 0124 (card delivery), 0134/0144 (compound leaves, denied-row Reconsider preserved).
- Tooling: no new libraries; Drizzle schema + existing repository ports; vitest as today.
- Recurring-findings tripwire: the RECURRING class `delivery-semantics @ jobs/execution-readiness` belongs to CARDSIMPLE-2's lifecycle area; if review flags it here, escalate per WORKFLOW.md instead of patching.

### Lessons in force

Recorded lessons that apply to this task's paths. A finding that contradicts one is not a defect unless it shows the lesson itself is wrong; say so explicitly instead of re-raising it.

- [medium] schema storage: Runtime state, jobs, control events, and memory use Postgres as the production storage model; schema or repository changes need repository tests and architecture/docs updates when contracts shift.
- [high] canonical-postgres-cutover: When replacing Postgres runtime schema in one cut, move active runtime persistence behind canonical Drizzle repositories/services in the same change; leaving schema-owned raw SQL or old table definitions creates drift and runtime failures after destructive migrations.
- [high] architecture boundaries: Keep provider-specific and channel-specific behavior behind adapters; domain and application code should depend on stable product concepts and ports, not SDK payloads or runtime wiring.
- [high] permission safety: Risky tool execution must pass through deterministic permission evaluation and sandbox policy before any provider callback or runner grants access.
- [medium] fleet-compose-rehearsal: Fleet compose rehearsal must run settings-seed through the normal Docker entrypoint so local auto-secrets are exported, and seed desired-state via the import service rather than the broad CLI bootstrap; the CLI bootstrap can close the shared runtime storage pool before settings import validation finishes. Docker-internal first-party Postgres hostnames need explicit plaintext allowance while real remote Postgres still requires sslmode=require.
- [medium] telegram-real-fs-ingestion-wait: Telegram media ingestion tests must wait for the observable delivery or file result when real filesystem writes are enabled; fixed microtask or timer counts return before descriptor-based writes finish.
- [low] prettier-before-factory-verify: Run the focused Prettier check after adding or reshaping TypeScript tests so the deterministic structural gate does not rediscover formatting drift.
- [medium] macos-sandbox-postgres-shared-memory: When Docker access is denied, a disposable local PostgreSQL 17 cluster can still be blocked during initdb because the sandbox rejects SysV shared memory; shared_memory_type and dynamic_shared_memory_type mmap options do not affect the bootstrap subprocess.
- [medium] unit-lane-nontermination: The full npm run test:unit lane can finish the LIVE-1 surfaces and then remain silent without a Vitest summary in this checkout; do not call it green without the exit code, and preserve focused lane evidence separately.
- [medium] managed-sandbox-junit-test-id: Managed command policy can reject required VITEST_JUNIT/FORGE_TEST_ID commands when the exact testcase identifier contains a literal greater-than separator. Report the wrapper lane as blocked and do not call it passing.
- [high] discord-progress-provider-deadline: Strict per-card Discord mutation exclusivity requires every progress edit and post to carry a bounded abort signal so one hung provider call cannot wedge the coalesced successor; preserve an overflow ambiguity fingerprint until a different payload's base edit actually completes.
- [low] managed-test-id-redirection-policy: Managed command policy can refuse the required FORGE_TEST_ID when its exact test name contains a greater-than character; report the policy refusal separately from focused test evidence.
- [medium] nonterminating-vitest-blast-radius: A jobs or runner directory-wide Vitest invocation can remain live without a summary or exit code in the managed environment; terminate it after bounded polling and report it as unverified, not green.
- [low] capfix-telegram-approval-test: Telegram permission-card tests that await a callback must explicitly configure isControlApproverAllowed; otherwise the promise stays pending until the test timeout.
- [medium] vitest-emfile-watcher: A focused Vitest selector can complete its test but still exit 1 when the macOS watcher hits EMFILE; treat this as blocked verification and rerun with the canonical wrapper or a watcher-safe environment.
- [high] JSONB persistence vs in-memory fakes: Postgres JSONB normalizes object key order and drops undefined; any equality check against persisted state (JSON.stringify ===) silently fails in prod while structuredClone-based fakes keep it green. Compare with util.isDeepStrictEqual and make repository fakes persist through a JSONB-faithful round trip (see test/unit/application/jsonb-round-trip.ts).
- [low] managed-env-prefix-policy: Managed execution can reject a required test when an inline environment assignment is the command prefix, reporting that the shell wrapper hides prefix inspection; invoke the same command through env so the executable prefix is visible, and report any remaining refusal separately.
- [low] managed-env-prefixed-test-policy: Managed command policy can refuse required Vitest commands when a leading environment assignment obscures the inspected prefix; preserve the refusal and run an equivalent direct Vitest JUnit command separately.
- [medium] Codex re-runs undo host-verified Postgres fixes: When a follow-up delegate carries a fix Codex cannot reproduce in its sandbox (Postgres-only hang or failure), state in the note that the earlier fixes are accepted and that only the named file may change, with the host-side proof; otherwise Codex reasons the fix away and reverts autoreview-accepted work (JOBPERM-3-T1 run 9).
- [high] Job permission card retire: persist delete failure before the receipt: When a retire delete fails, the provider delivery must surface deleteFailedAt through the partial-delivery error BEFORE any receipt call (Telegram partialFallback pattern); the receipt edit runs on the next retry. A logging-only onDeleteFailure lets a crash between delete and edit re-issue the delete.
- [high] Teams job permission card receipt must stay retryable: With a recorded activity id, a failed or unavailable updateAdaptiveCard must rethrow so the retire revision is retried; sending a new text receipt instead leaves the old actionable card in place and the persisted receiptMessageId makes it unrepairable.
- [high] rail-ASK outcomes must run every named decision stage before the tail: In the coordinator a base rail ASK (including the reviewed-rule-allows-but-rail-asks branch) must still flow through conditional trusted-root handling and the classifier-cache read before invoking tail(context); an early return there ignores learned trusted roots for reviewed-rule requests and skips cached verdicts for the newly relaxable out_of_trusted_root / read-only find cases (autoreview P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:172). Cover the rail-ASK path in the stage-order test.
- [medium] cached classifier allows flow through the rail merge, not around it: For a relaxable rail ASK the coordinator must pass an existing cached classifier allow through the typed tail/merge path (same lane guard and rail provenance) instead of discarding it with '&& !railDecision' and re-consulting the classifier — autoreview r2 P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:219: a valid cached verdict was ignored, causing fresh consults and prompts when the classifier is unavailable.
- [medium] trusted-root stage never invokes the tail itself: resolveTrustedRootStage must only prepare the trusted-root prompt/learning state and continue through the remembered-allow and classifier-cache stages to the single tail invocation, with any persistent-root writeback after that decision — autoreview r2 P2 at permission-decision-coordinator.ts:320: with a candidate root but no learned grant it invoked the tail directly, skipping the authoritative order and forcing a live classifier call despite a cached verdict. Pin it in the stage-order test.
- [high] cached classifier allows are consumed only in classifier-eligible lanes: Gate cached-verdict consumption and any auto-allow from it on the lane: a classifier allow cached while in auto must never be reused after switching to permissionMode ask (ask mode has no classifier authority), and auto_strict keeps its veto behaviour — autoreview r3 P1: with every analyzed rail ASK now reaching the cache stage, an ordinary single-file delete cached in auto was executed as auto_classifier in ask mode without a prompt. Add an ask-lane cached-allow negative leaf.
- [high] coordinator cache stage under a rail ASK: Under a rail ASK the classifier-verdict cache may be read ONLY when the signal is one of the two overridable ones (out_of_trusted_root, unsupported_meta_executor) AND the lane is interactive auto, because only the tail merge can consume it there. Every other rail ASK (destructive, secret, escape, family-rule hit) must skip the cache read entirely, exactly as before this story: ipc-interaction-handler.test.ts pins that a destructive ASK never calls getClassifierVerdict while the intact command is still written back. Run the full unit suite (verify.py), not only the nine T1 suites, before ending a run.

### Reviewer focus

- LAYERS (load-bearing; scripts/architecture-map.json:94-120): app/ and runtime/ are the runtime layer and may import application/ and shared/, never channels/. The pure latch + copy is an APPLICATION module (application/permissions/permission-judge-outage-latch.ts, imports nothing from runtime); the process-wide instance, the synthetic wiring_missing prompt result and the notice sender live in the NEW RUNTIME module runtime/permission-judge-outage.ts; both callers make calls into it and send through their already-injected sendMessage port with { threadId, providerAccountId }. Any channel import in the diff is a blocking finding.
- LATCH (AC1 normative; owner ruling story plan line 167): process-local, in-memory, keyed by app id + provider account id + conversation jid; noticeDue only on the FIRST unavailable per key; answered clears; skipped never touches it; clearAll() is the test hook. No persistence. wiring_missing is a FAILURE CODE in the permission-classifier.ts string union, not a status, produced ONLY for an eligible lane whose wiring is absent; an unavailable result is NEVER written to the verdict cache. JOB LANES follow 0157: notice to the job conversation before the terminal job decision; the offline reason rides the decision.
- COPY (AC2, AC3 normative): the notice is exactly 'My safety judge is offline, so I'll check with you more than usual until it's back.' sent BEFORE the first offline card; the card reason is exactly 'Asking because my safety judge is offline.' on request.decisionReason. Both strings are exported from the latch module and nowhere else.
- NO TAP STORM (AC4 normative; AF-AC5): deterministic read-only allows short-circuit inside the classifier before any LLM path and never notify; an uncovered read asks at most once per request; Allow with remember still writes the memory row offline. Scheduled jobs keep deterministic denial + card recovery.
- INVARIANCE (AC5 normative; AF-AC6): the new suite is a table over EXISTING harness fixtures with expected tuples copied verbatim; the only new column is the unavailable stub; no earlier-owned test is edited. Test titles must equal the required_tests ids verbatim.

### Settled — do not relitigate

The following are accepted: the story plan's decisions and rulings, and the contracts of tasks already sealed in this story. A finding that contradicts one is a proposal to change a decision, which belongs in a decision record, not in this review; do not raise it as a defect. Rejected findings from earlier rounds are ledgered as lessons below.

#### Story plan — Decisions

- `docs/decisions/0153-learned-decisions-project-into-job-grants.md` (proposed → accept at approval): restates 0121's invariant — a job's outcome is a pure function of declared grants — and widens the declared-grant set by exactly one host-owned deterministic input, active `human_decision` records, evaluated live per request and revocable; the classifier is still never invoked for autonomous runs.
- `docs/decisions/0154-human-decision-memory-generic-scope.md` (proposed → accept at approval; explicitly AMENDS 0118's unresolved-identity rule ("shared grant; no downgrade", `0118:45-47`) for `human_decision` records only — unresolved person persists nothing and acts once — and AMENDS 0052 and 0121 for the all-mode attachment birthright — 0121's "grant miss denies" rule gains one input-gated birthright exception, stated in 0154's Decision text, no separate record): the human-decision store is a distinct record kind consulted before the classifier in interactive auto only; Allow AND No are learned with a generic scope (broadest-safe default: reads → kind anywhere; writes/destructive → exact, file-write exact = path only per owner ruling); Just-this-once is never learned; rails bump and Forget invalidate; place reuses `resolveTrustedRootStage`. Rejected: exact-hash-only learning (cannot end shell-heavy tapping).
- `docs/decisions/0155-default-allow-gantry-tools-interactive-auto.md` (ACCEPTED by Ravi 2026-09-04; OWNER RULING 2026-09-03): in interactive auto, gantry-native tools auto-allow by default (browser included) and only the closed high-risk rows ask — destructive/protected writes, the registry's scheduler-mutation and admin-mutation exports; non-own-destination messaging is HIGH by principle with no such tool today (0052 birthright unchanged) — with ambiguous shapes routed to the classifier; auto-allows are visible through typed provenance and the audit trail, not `/permissions`; re-calibrates the conservative static buckets of 0043/#212 (`gantry-tool-risk.ts:98`) and AMENDS 0052's browser reading (browser network side-effects auto-allow by explicit owner choice; 0052's shell-egress and secret floors untouched) without touching the shared rails, ask mode, auto_strict or jobs. Browser file matrix, exactly: raw-path source (`file_attach` with a path, or `file_upload` with a path-type source) in-workspace LOW, outside-workspace HIGH, protected HIGH, secret HIGH, malformed ambiguous; artifact-sourced `file_upload` LOW. `file` is judged by the discriminated per-action predicate (every host-valid defaulted shape LOW; protected virtual targets HIGH).
- Load-bearing, unchanged: 0040 (once/this-folder/standing scopes — generic scope generalizes "this-folder" into "place"), 0043 (deterministic facts in rails, risk in classification — the attachment birthright is a deterministic fact: host-validated origin), 0052 (birthright self-surface — the attachment-already-in-the-conversation birthright is an input-gated addition to that set, recorded in 0154's Decision text as an explicit amendment of 0052 and 0121; send_message out of scope), 0054/0107 (typed provenance for every new allow/deny), 0121 (no classifier on autonomous runs), 0124 (card delivery), 0134/0144 (compound leaves, denied-row Reconsider preserved).
- Tooling: no new libraries; Drizzle schema + existing repository ports; vitest as today.
- Recurring-findings tripwire: the RECURRING class `delivery-semantics @ jobs/execution-readiness` belongs to CARDSIMPLE-2's lifecycle area; if review flags it here, escalate per WORKFLOW.md instead of patching.

### Lessons in force

Recorded lessons that apply to this task's paths. A finding that contradicts one is not a defect unless it shows the lesson itself is wrong; say so explicitly instead of re-raising it.

- [medium] schema storage: Runtime state, jobs, control events, and memory use Postgres as the production storage model; schema or repository changes need repository tests and architecture/docs updates when contracts shift.
- [high] architecture boundaries: Keep provider-specific and channel-specific behavior behind adapters; domain and application code should depend on stable product concepts and ports, not SDK payloads or runtime wiring.
